brief.subject: CFPB targets debanking; who gets approved for secured cards
brief.headline: CFPB Opens New Push on Debanking by Large Banks; Secured Card Approval Data
brief.dek: The CFPB is acting on debanking findings from the OCC, and new application data shows how credit scores affect secured card approvals.
brief.lede: The CFPB has launched a new initiative against debanking by large banks, building on findings from the OCC.

sections.heading: CFPB takes aim at debanking
bullets: The CFPB announced a new initiative on 2026-10-14 targeting debanking by large banks.
It builds on debanking cases uncovered by the OCC, the federal regulator of national banks.
The bureau frames it as protecting people and businesses cut off over constitutionally protected rights.
If a bank has closed your account without clear reason, keep your letters and records.

sections.heading: Secured card approvals by credit score
bullets: New application data breaks down secured credit card approval rates by credit score band.
Secured cards require a deposit and are often a first step for rebuilding damaged credit.
Checking where your score falls can help you avoid applications likely to be denied.

brief.seo_description: CFPB launches an initiative on debanking by large banks, plus data on how credit scores affect secured credit card approvals.
